## What We Did

I learned how to create and stylize ggplots, and account for uncertainty using moe calculations. 

## Key Concepts

1. Asombe's quartet: Four different data visualizations with the same x and y mean. Plot is a mapping from coloumns in the the data to visual properties on the page. ("Grammar of Graphics") "GG". 

2. ggplot translation
  Data              ->          Page(Canvas)
  estimate                      position on the y-axis
  population                    position on the x-axis
  reliability                   color 
  moe                           size

3. components of a ggplot 
  a. ggplot(data) -> creates a blank canvas
  b. aes...() aesthetic mappings: NO DECORATING, just business
  c. geom_*(): the shape / type of chart 

4. how to make a ggplot 
  ggplot(tract_data) + 
    aes(x = population, y = moe_pct) +
    geompoint()
    
    insideaes()                       not inside
    aes(color = reliability)          geom_point("blue")
                                      decorations 
    
    example: ggplot(county_data) +
             aes(x = estimate, y = population) +
             geom_point(color = "blue")
             
            * look up R color codes 
            
    what I want to know               geom
    how a variable is spread          geom_histogram()
    how do two variables relate       geom_point()
    how do groups compare             geom_boxplot() / geom_col()
    how do things change over time    geom_line()
    how uncertain is a value          geom_errorbars()
    
5. coefficent of variation (cv)
  relative measure of sampling error
  = (standard error / estimate) * 100 
  
  cv thresholds
  low = 15% -> high reliability 
  medium = 15% - 30% 
  high = 30%+ -> high sampling error 
             
6. derived uncertainty
  pov. rate = (# in poverty ± moe) / (total pop ± moe)
  moe_sum -> adding estimates together 
  moe_prop() -> one estimate as share of another
  moe_ratio() -> (pop #) / (HH Income) 
    *one is not a subset of another 
    
7. change over time 
  a. compare non-overlapping intervals 
    2019 - 2023 , 2018 - 2022 DOES NOT WORK 
    2014 - 2018 , 2019 - 2023 DOES WORK 
    
    standard error of difference (SEdiff)
 
    confidence interval of change
      difference ± (1.645 * SEdiff)
